text: In August 2014 Bank of America agreed to a $16.65 billion settlement, including $7 billion in consumer relief, with the US Justice Department, other federal agencies and several states over mortgage-backed securities and other mortgage business leading up to and during the financial crisis.

source.name: US Department of Justice: Bank of America to Pay $16.65 Billion in Historic Justice Department Settlement for Financial Fraud Leading up to and During the Financial Crisis
source.quote: the Department of Justice has reached a $16.65 billion settlement with Bank of America Corporation – the largest civil settlement with a single entity in American history

additionalSources.name: Bank of America Corporation: Form 10-Q for the quarter ended 30 September 2014 (SEC EDGAR)
additionalSources.quote: Under the DoJ Settlement, the Corporation agreed to pay a total of $9.65 billion in cash and provide $7.0 billion worth of consumer relief.

additionalSources.name: US Securities and Exchange Commission: Bank of America Admits Disclosure Failures to Settle SEC Charges (press release 2014-172)
additionalSources.quote: a major global settlement announced today by the U.S. Department of Justice in which Bank of America will pay $16.65 billion to resolve various investigations
